increments.title: A correction round's researcher is sent to its own previous plan
increments.goal: A correction round's researcher prompt names the previous round's research step of the same increment and its plan field, and instructs the researcher to read it out of the run state before planning the fix; the pages that describe what such a researcher reads say so too, and a test turns red when the prompt stops naming it.
criteria: A correction round's researcher prompt names the research step of the round before for the same increment, and instructs the researcher to read that step's plan out of the run state before it plans the fix.
The prompt names that step and its field and copies no plan text into itself.
The step the prompt names belongs to the increment being worked and never to another increment.
Where the increment's previous round dispatched no researcher, the prompt names no such step and stays valid.
Every page that describes what a correction round's researcher reads describes this too.
A test turns red when the prompt no longer names the previous round's plan.

return.plan:
# What gets built

A correction round's researcher dispatch gains one more read: the research step
of the round *before*, with `--fields plan`. No plan text is copied into the
prompt — the read is the channel, exactly as the codemap read already is. Two
files change under the implementer's hand: `workflows/agile-loop.js` (the prompt
builder) and `agents/researcher.md` (the only page that describes what a
correction round's researcher reads). `test-repo.sh` is the test-author's file
for this increment; the implementer changes nothing in it.

Line numbers below are as of commit `ac6e705`.

## 1. `workflows/agile-loop.js`

### (a) A per-round label, mirroring `previousTestsLabel`

The script already tracks "what the round before left behind" for the
test-author, with a pair of variables: `testsLabel`, set inside the round, and
`previousTestsLabel`, copied from it at the top of the next round. Build the
plan label the same way, and nothing new:

- Inside the increment loop, beside `let planLabel = ''`, `let testsLabel = ''`
  and `let previousTestsLabel = ''` (lines 1104-1106), add
  `let previousPlanLabel = ''`. It is declared **inside** the increment loop and
  never at module scope beside `lastChecks` (line 1018): `lastChecks`
  deliberately crosses increment boundaries because a command judges whatever
  code is in front of it, while a plan is written against one increment's
  criteria, and a researcher sent to another increment's plan is sent to a design
  that is not its own.
- At the top of the round loop, immediately before `previousTestsLabel =
  testsLabel` (line 1110), add `previousPlanLabel = planLabel`.
- In the `if (directFix || directRound)` branch, beside `testsLabel = ''`
  (line 1135), add `planLabel = ''`. This reset is what makes the round-before
  rule true in the middle of an attempt: a round that dispatched no researcher
  must leave no plan label behind, so a round 2 that follows a direct-fix round 1
  names nothing rather than reaching back over it to round 0. In that branch
  `planLabel` is read by nobody — the implementer's `directFix` and `directRound`
  arms of the prompt never touch it — so clearing it costs nothing.

### (b) The read itself

In the researcher dispatch (lines 1140-1167), inside the
`round === 0 ? '' : readBlock(...)` expression, add a third entry to the list,
between the `review ... findings` line and the `tests ... openQuestions` line:

```js
previousPlanLabel
  ? readStep(
      task.id,
      previousPlanLabel,
      'plan',
      `the plan you wrote for the round before: correct that design instead of ` +
        `deriving it again.`,
    )
  : '',
```

Three things about it are load-bearing:

- The increment id passed to `readStep` is `task.id`, the increment being worked,
  and the label is `previousPlanLabel`, which only ever holds a label of that same
  increment because the variable is declared inside the increment loop.
- The field list is `plan` alone — not `plan,moduleMap`, not the whole step. The
  issue settles this: the findings and the open questions already reach this
  researcher by their own reads, and the `moduleMap` is this round's to rewrite.
- The guard is what criterion 4 rests on. `.filter(Boolean)` at the end of the
  list (line 1162) already drops an empty string, so a round whose predecessor
  dispatched no researcher renders a `readBlock` with the remaining lines and
  stays a valid prompt.

Because the whole expression sits behind `round === 0 ? '' : ...`, round 0 is
untouched and no first-round researcher is sent anywhere.

### (c) The comment above the dispatch

Lines 1138-1139 read: "What the round before left for this one, all of it in the
state: the review's findings, and the questions the test-author left open."
Rewrite it so it names the third thing and why it is a read rather than a copy:
the plan the round before wrote is the design this round corrects, it is the
largest thing any agent of this run produces, and the state is where it already
is. Name the empty branch in the same comment: a round whose predecessor
dispatched no researcher names no plan step at all.

### What must not change in this file

- No schema and no payload changes. `PLAN` (line 313), `PLAN_PAYLOAD` (line 503),
  `INDEX_STEP` and `STATE` stay exactly as they are: the plan text never enters
  this script in the first place — the researcher's structured return carries
  only `needsTests`, `checks`, `breaks`, `unbreakable`, `questions` and `summary`
  — which is why criterion 2's "copies no plan text" is a property to keep, not
  one to build.
- The test-author dispatch (lines 1180-1194) keeps reading `planLabel` — this
  round's plan — and gains nothing.
- The implementer dispatch (lines 1200-1256) is untouched; the issue puts the
  other roles' prompts out of scope.

## 2. `agents/researcher.md`

Two edits, both in the page's own voice, and no rule stated twice.

### (a) `## Correction rounds` (lines 118-128)

Its first two sentences today name two reads: the review's findings and the
test-author's open questions. Add the third as a rule keyed to an observable
predicate — the prompt either names the step or it does not — with each branch
stated on its own, per `.claude/rules/authoring.md`'s last row. Write these two
sentences **verbatim**, as the second paragraph of that section (the test greps
for the first of them):

    Where your prompt names the research step of the round before, read its
    `plan` first: it is the design you already wrote, and this round corrects it
    instead of deriving it again from the codebase. Where it names no such step,
    the round before dispatched no researcher and there is nothing to correct.

Leave the section's closing sentences as they stand — "Nothing carries over from
the earlier rounds — the return you record is what binds now, and a case you do
not repeat in it is not asked for again." That sentence already says the thing
the new rule must not contradict and must not repeat: what you read is last
round's design, but what you record still has to stand on its own, because the
implementer of this round reads this round's step and no other.

### (b) The frontmatter `description` (line 3)

It says the researcher is run "again for each correction round, where it reads
the reviewer's findings out of the run state and turns them into a correction
plan". That is a description of what such a researcher reads, so it names this
too: make the clause read "where it reads the reviewer's findings and the plan
the round before wrote out of the run state and turns them into a correction
plan". Keep the rest of the description as it is — it names an occasion and
hands back a result, and must not start walking through steps.

Two phrases stay off this page whatever the wording: `counts as tested` and
`dependency footprint`. `test-repo.sh` asserts the shared brief is their only
owner among agent pages, and using either turns those cases red.

## 3. What is deliberately not touched

- `README.md`. Its researcher row (line 81) says what the role produces and its
  loop diagram (line 61) says a correction round exists; neither describes what
  such a researcher reads, so criterion 5 does not reach them.
- `hooks/read-barrier.mjs`. Its `RULES` table gates the implementer, the reviewer
  and the test-author; the researcher is deliberately absent, so its read of its
  own previous `plan` passes without a change there.
- `skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md`. It says how any agent takes its brief, and never
  what a correction round's researcher reads.
- The other roles' prompts, the codemap, and the researcher's return schema — all
  out of scope by the issue.

## Rejected alternatives

- **Copying the previous plan into the prompt.** It is the largest thing any
  agent of a run produces (the issue measures 23,700 characters per researcher
  step), and the run state already carries it. Copying would also break criterion
  2 and put content back into a script that has been emptied of it on purpose.
- **Reading the last researcher step rather than the round before's.** A single
  module-scope "last plan label", carried the way `lastChecks` is, is fewer lines
  — and is what criteria 3 and 4 exist to forbid: it hands an increment worked
  after a direct one, or a round worked after a direct-fix one, a plan written
  for something else.
- **`--fields plan,moduleMap`.** The module map is the field the researcher is
  told to correct where the codemap is wrong; carrying last round's would invite
  a copy instead of a fresh reading, and the issue names the plan alone.

# Whether

Tests. Every criterion but the last is a fact about a string the workflow builds
or a sentence a page carries, and both are checkable.

Every case below lands in `/home/user/uroboros/test-repo.sh` and nowhere else.
Do not touch `workflows/agile-loop.js` or `agents/researcher.md`: the cases are
written against the behaviour the plan describes, and the implementer builds it.

# What — the cases, by criterion

## Criterion 1 — the prompt names the round-before's research step and orders the read

- **1.1** — mode `w10` (exists; one full increment, `review:i1.0` returns
  `verdictReturnWithFinding`, so exactly one correction round runs) — the
  `research:i1.1` dispatch prompt → contains `readStep('i1', 'research:i1.0',
  'plan')`, i.e. the exact string
  `steps docs/issues/x/backlog.json i1 research:i1.0 --fields plan` — break:
  delete the `previousPlanLabel ? readStep(...) : ''` entry from the correction
  `readBlock` list in the researcher dispatch of `workflows/agile-loop.js`.

## Criterion 2 — it names the step and its field, and copies no plan text

- **2.1** — mode `w10` — the same asserted string as 1.1 carries `--fields plan`,
  so the field is pinned by it; the driver's standing per-call assertion that no
  prompt reads a step without `--fields` (already at the top of `main`) covers
  every other mode — break: change the new read to name no fields
  (`readStep(task.id, previousPlanLabel, '', ...)`), which the standing
  assertion and 2.1 both catch.
- **2.2** — every mode, as a standing per-call assertion — the shared
  `planReturn` fixture gains a `plan: 'MARKER-PLAN-TEXT'` property (the two
  fixtures derived from it with `Object.assign` inherit it), `MARKER-PLAN-TEXT`
  joins `DISJOINT_MARKERS`, and no prompt of any dispatch in any mode contains
  `MARKER-PLAN-TEXT` → no prompt carries plan text — break: interpolate the
  researcher's returned plan into the correction prompt (append the round-before
  return's `plan` to the `readBlock` intro) instead of naming the read.

## Criterion 3 — the step named belongs to the increment being worked

- **3.1** (positive) — mode `w10` — the assertion of 1.1 names `i1` and
  `research:i1.0` while increment i1 is being worked — break: as 1.1.
- **3.2** (negative) — new mode `w37`, fixture `{ stateReturn: noState,
  decomposeReturn: decomposeReturnMixed, researchReturn: planReturn, verdictFor:
  (label) => (label === 'review:i2.0' ? verdictReturnWithFinding :
  verdictReturnClean) }` — i1 is full and clean, i2 is the planner's `direct`
  increment whose round-0 review files one non-direct finding, so i2's round 1
  is a full correction round whose own previous round dispatched no researcher.
  Expected labels: `load-state`, `decompose`, `research:i1.0`, `tests:i1.0`,
  `implement:i1.0`, `review:i1.0`, `replan:i1`, `implement:i2.0`, `review:i2.0`,
  `research:i2.1`, `tests:i2.1`, `implement:i2.1`, `review:i2.1`, `replan:i2`,
  `publish`. Assert the `research:i2.1` prompt contains no occurrence of
  `research:i1` at all → the correction round is never sent to another
  increment's plan — break: carry the last researcher's label at module scope
  beside `lastChecks` (one `lastPlanLabel`, set wherever a researcher runs, used
  in place of the per-increment `previousPlanLabel`), which lets i1's label
  survive into i2 and renders
  `steps docs/issues/x/backlog.json i2 research:i1.0 --fields plan`.

## Criterion 4 — no researcher in the previous round: no such step, still valid

- **4.1** — mode `w37` (same fixture and label assertion as 3.2) — the
  `research:i2.1` prompt matches no `steps docs/issues/x/backlog.json i2
  research:` read at all, and still contains `readStep('i2', 'review:i2.0',
  'findings')`, and the label sequence above is unchanged → the prompt names no
  plan step and stays valid — break: drop the `previousPlanLabel ? ... : ''`
  guard and render the read unconditionally, which emits a read whose label is
  empty.
- **4.2** — new mode `w38`, fixture `{ stateReturn: noState, decomposeReturn:
  decomposeReturnOne, researchReturn: planReturn, verdictFor: (label) => (label
  === 'review:i1.0' ? verdictReturnWithDirectFinding : label === 'review:i1.1' ?
  verdictReturnWithFinding : verdictReturnClean) }` — one full increment whose
  round-0 review files an all-direct finding (round 1 is a direct-fix round with
  no researcher) and whose round-1 review files an ordinary one (round 2 is a
  full round). Expected labels: `load-state`, `decompose`, `research:i1.0`,
  `tests:i1.0`, `implement:i1.0`, `review:i1.0`, `implement:i1.1`, `review:i1.1`,
  `research:i1.2`, `tests:i1.2`, `implement:i1.2`, `review:i1.2`, `replan:i1`,
  `publish`. Assert the `research:i1.2` prompt matches no
  `steps docs/issues/x/backlog.json i1 research:` read — in particular not
  `research:i1.0`, the plan two rounds back — and still contains
  `readStep('i1', 'review:i1.1', 'findings')` — break: delete `planLabel = ''`
  from the `if (directFix || directRound)` branch of the round loop, so round 0's
  label survives the direct-fix round and round 2 is sent back to it.

## Criterion 5 — every page that describes these reads describes this one

Two `ok`/`no` cases under one new `echo "=== ..."` heading, placed beside the
existing researcher-page cases (the block that starts at
`=== the mutation standard has one owner`, lines 473-585), each with a comment
naming its break, in that block's style.

- **5.1** — `agents/researcher.md`, collapsed to one line the way the existing
  `break_researcher_collapsed` case does it (`tr '\n' ' ' <page | tr -s ' '`) →
  contains, verbatim, `Where your prompt names the research step of the round
  before, read its \`plan\` first` — break: delete that sentence from the page's
  `## Correction rounds` section.
- **5.2** — the `description:` line of the same page's frontmatter → contains
  `the plan the round before wrote` — break: revert the description's correction-
  round clause to naming the reviewer's findings alone.

## Criterion 6 — a test turns red when the prompt stops naming the plan

- **6.1** — case 1.1 is that test, and its break is the deletion of the read from
  the dispatch. No second case: a criterion satisfied by the existence of another
  criterion's case is satisfied by that case running.

## Criterion 7 — `bash test.sh` exits 0

No case of its own: the command in **What counts as done** is the executable
check, and it turns red when any case above, or any other suite, fails.

# How

- **Level** — unit, all of them. The driver loads `workflows/agile-loop.js`
  in-process (`new AsyncFunction`) with a stubbed `agent` and asserts on the
  prompts it built; the page cases are greps. Nothing spawns a run.
- **File** — `/home/user/uroboros/test-repo.sh`, the only test file this
  increment touches.
- **Framework** — plain bash with the file's own `ok`/`no` counters, plus the
  embedded Node driver in the `cat >"$driver_tmp/driver.js" <<'JS'` heredoc
  (lines 809-2225), which has its own `assertTrue` / `assertEqualArrays` and uses
  no test framework.
- **Command that runs just that file** — `bash test-repo.sh`, from
  `/home/user/uroboros`.

## The suite's conventions, because there is no doc for them

There is no `CLAUDE.md` governing `test-repo.sh`: the repository root has none,
and `hooks/CLAUDE.md` documents only the two `node --test` suites under
`hooks/`. Do not create one — a `CLAUDE.md` at the root would load into every
session in this checkout and be inherited by every subagent, which
`.claude/rules/agents.md` exists to prevent, and every rule page in this
repository is path-scoped for exactly that reason. What the suite does instead is
in its own comments; these are the conventions the new cases follow:

- A driver case is three edits: a `case 'wN':` returning its fixture in
  `contextFor` (line 1160), a `} else if (mode === 'wN') {` branch in the
  assertion chain, and a `run_driver "$wf" wN "$wf_name: <what it proves>"` line
  in the `for wf in ...` registration loop (line 2237). `w36` is the highest
  number in use, so the new modes are `w37` and `w38`.
- Each mode branch opens with a comment saying what case it is and why it exists;
  each assertion message states what went wrong, never what was expected.
- Build every read string with the driver's `readStep(id, label, fields)` helper
  (line 864) or with the `'steps ' + STATE_PATH + ...` form it is made of — never
  hand-write the path.
- A new marker string joins `DISJOINT_MARKERS` (line 832); the driver's first
  assertion proves no marker contains another, so it must not be a substring of,
  or contain, an existing one.
- Fixtures are shared module-level constants (`planReturn`, `decomposeReturnMixed`,
  `verdictReturnWithDirectFinding`, `verdictReturnWithFinding`,
  `verdictReturnClean`), reused rather than copied; a mode that needs a variant
  builds it with `Object.assign({}, base, {...})`.
- Page cases sit under an `echo` heading of their own, use `ok`/`no`, and carry a
  comment naming the production change that turns them red.

## Faked and real

The driver fakes exactly one thing — the `agent` function — and runs the real
workflow source against it. Nothing else is stubbed; the page cases read the real
files.

# What counts as done

    bash test.sh

One command, run from `/home/user/uroboros`. Nothing else runs: the two new
driver modes, the two amended ones and the two page cases are all inside
`test-repo.sh`, which `test.sh` runs first, and criterion 7 asks for the whole
suite anyway.

# What is already red

Nothing was run, and the list is unrun. No decision in this plan turns on a fact
only a run can settle: the prompt shape, the round-loop variables, the fixture
harness and the page's wording were all settled by reading `workflows/agile-loop.js`,
`test-repo.sh` and `agents/researcher.md`. The first run belongs to whoever runs
it downstream.
